key_insight: A multi-objective Pareto-front optimization produces content-adaptive, quality-monotonic bitrate ladders for VVC that jointly trade off bitrate, visual quality, and decoding complexity—enabling more efficient adaptive streaming than fixed ladders.
problem_solved: Fixed or single-objective bitrate ladders fail to balance bitrate, quality, and decoder complexity across diverse content; this work finds optimal, content-dependent operating points that respect quality monotonicity and practical decoding constraints.
method: Formulate per-content multi-objective optimization over bitrate, objective quality (e.g., VMAF/PSNR) and decoding complexity.
Compute the Pareto front of candidate encodes and extract a quality-monotonic, content-adaptive bitrate ladder from Pareto-optimal points.
Integrate the selected ladder into VVC streaming and evaluate trade-offs vs. conventional ladders on rate–quality–complexity metrics.
impact: Provides a practical method to generate smarter bitrate ladders that reduce bandwidth or decoder load while preserving perceived quality—useful for researchers and engineers designing adaptive streaming systems, codec-aware encoders, or ML-driven rate-control policies.
visual_elements: Pareto-front scatter plot (bitrate vs. quality vs. complexity) highlighting selected ladder points
Before/after bitrate-ladder diagram showing fixed vs. content-adaptive, quality-monotonic levels
Pipeline flowchart: content analysis → multi-objective optimizer → Pareto selection → VVC ladder deployment
Bar/heatmap comparison of bitrate, quality, and decoder-complexity savings across content classes
paper_title: Multi-Objective Pareto-Front Optimization for Efficient Adaptive VVC Streaming
paper_authors: Angeliki Katsenou, Vignesh V. Menon, Guoda Laurinaviciute, Benjamin Bross, Detlev Marpe
